problem_text:
A logistics company is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vehicle. The available containers are:

* Container 1: size 40 cubic meters, revenue $17
* Container 2: size 19 cubic meters, revenue $68
* Container 3: size 11 cubic meters, revenue $150
* Container 4: size 13 cubic meters, revenue $272
* Container 5: size 36 cubic meters, revenue $187
* Container 6: size 29 cubic meters, revenue $55
* Container 7: size 27 cubic meters, revenue $267
* Container 8: size 35 cubic meters, revenue $219
* Container 9: size 8 cubic meters, revenue $51
* Container 10: size 38 cubic meters, revenue $247
* Container 11: size 21 cubic meters, revenue $99
* Container 12: size 19 cubic meters, revenue $133
* Container 13: size 41 cubic meters, revenue $233
* Container 14: size 44 cubic meters, revenue $156
* Container 15: size 3 cubic meters, revenue $21
* Container 16: size 1 cubic meter, revenue $147

The vehicle has a maximum capacity of 269 cubic meters. Choose the combination of containers that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this capacity limit. Each container must be either fully accepted or rejected.
